conventions.convention: The observation space is R^H with its cylinder sigma-algebra. Process linearity holds in L²(P), hence represents almost-sure equalities rather than pointwise identities of all sample paths.

H is a separable real Hilbert space, epsilon is strictly positive, and finite orthonormal tuples have independent standard-normal noise values. N(a, sigma²) denotes the affine-image scalar law, including zero variance.
The supplied complete orthonormal basis is indexed from 1, is finite or countably infinite, and may be empty for the zero space. Finite projections become the identity after the last basis vector.

Reconstruction is in mean square. The measurable reconstruction map additionally gives almost-sure equality for each fixed parameter and finite list of test vectors; exceptional sets may depend on that list. No simultaneous path identity over H is asserted.

Countable choice is required for the cited negative-Sobolev Borel Gaussian realization with delta > 1/2. Given the process and indexed basis, the coordinate and cylinder-equivalence arguments use least natural-number indices without additional choice.

load_bearing.statement: For a supplied isonormal Gaussian process on a separable real Hilbert space H, a signal map K:X→H, a nonempty parameter set Θ⊆X, and epsilon > 0, define Y_x(g)=⟨Kx,g⟩+epsilon Z(g). The experiment consists of its laws on R^H with the evaluation-generated cylinder sigma-algebra; an H-valued sample or continuous path is not asserted.

For a fixed complete finite or countably infinite orthonormal basis, including the empty basis of the zero space, Y_x(u_j) are independent N(⟨Kx,u_j⟩,epsilon²) coordinates. Their finite linear combinations reconstruct every fixed observation functional in L²(P). Parameter-independent measurable maps S and T satisfy S_*P_x=Q_x, T_*Q_x=P_x, and S∘T=id. For the specified L²([0,1]) bases, countable choice and delta > 1/2 give a Borel Gaussian H(delta) realization, which is not L²-valued in infinite dimension.

Bounding the deterministic contribution to mean-square reconstruction error.
The weighted coefficient carrier H(delta) and continuous embedding of L²([0,1]).
Under countable choice, the specified Gaussian coordinates give a Borel H(delta) realization for delta > 1/2 and fail to be L²-valued.
The exact choice assumption inherited by the negative-Sobolev realization.
Summable probability bounds for reconstruction errors along the least-index subsequence.
Almost-sure convergence of the explicitly chosen scalar reconstructions without independence.
Measurability of each reconstruction coordinate, its convergence set, and its default-zero extension.
Extending equality on finite evaluation cylinders to equality of field sampling laws.

seams_checked.note: The sequence-model definition restricts the functional experiment to the separable closed range with its supplied complete singular basis. Dividing coordinate observations by positive singular values gives the stated independent Gaussian laws. Zero noise is defined separately.

The mixture and detection arguments use independent scalar Gaussian coordinates after the stated rescaling. Their uses preserve positive noise and do not infer an H-valued white-noise observation or a simultaneous path identity.

The algorithm and risk results explicitly use weak isonormal observations and independent singular coordinates. Filtered X-valued estimator limits are established separately; they are not identified with unfiltered white noise. Countable choice is retained.

Probe means, variances, and scalar normal laws agree with the isonormal definition. Posterior statements explicitly allow exceptional sets depending on the fixed feature and supply stronger Bayesian and operator hypotheses separately. The zero probe is treated as deterministic.

This is a contextual page prerequisite. The actual tomography experiment is a finite Bernoulli-link experiment with explicitly defined finite sampling laws; it does not cite white noise as a logical supplier or assert Gaussian equivalence.

The page uses a general translated-noise experiment with measurable translations. Its indistinguishability result assumes equality of sampling laws directly and does not strengthen any white-noise conclusion.

The contraction results use positive-noise Gaussian sequence laws through the sequence-model prerequisite. Data remain in the product-Borel sequence space; prior and posterior support on ell² are separate assertions with trace hypotheses.

The coverage definition is for general experiments. The open problem uses independent scalar Gaussian sequence observations with positive noise n^(-1/2), without asserting an ell²-valued data sample or using an unproved coverage claim as a supplier.
